stem: A technician corrected a small hose obstruction and began work. Ten minutes later, water is now spreading toward a powered device with visible cord damage. What is the strongest next action?
choices: Continue because the original pre-task check already passed
Reassess the changed condition, stop the affected work, control exposure within authorization, and escalate the electrical hazard
Move the hose again and ignore the damaged cord unless the breaker trips
Open the device to determine whether the cord damage is only cosmetic
rationale: A pre-task check is not permanent clearance. When conditions change, the technician reassesses the new hazard state, stops affected work as needed, uses only authorized controls, and escalates electrical conditions rather than troubleshooting beyond role authority.
